Best Plant App (Free!). I have tried almost every plant identification app out there. This is the only one I absolutely love. And it’s free! Aside from that, though, I love this app because you can add pics of your own to try to identify. Instead of just throwing you something it might be and saying “this is what this is” like most other apps, this one lists it out. Depending on your pic quality depends on the percentage of plant comparisons it gives you, however, it seems to be no less than 95% right every time. There was only one plant I scanned that wasn’t what they listed (and I knew that is what that plant was), but my pic was a really bad shot, so it was probably my fault. I’ve been using this app for a couple months (and I am constantly doing something on it). I absolutely love it. It’s also community open, so if the app isn’t sure what it could be, they’ll put it in the community for other educated people to add their input. You can look species up by region, family, genius, or just by name/characteristics. I’m learning so much about the region I live in simply by looking at the plants and flora and weeds in that specific region. I love how it lists other names the plant is known by, a world map of where it can be found, and photos of it all. The photos!!! You can identify or search something via leaf, flower, bark/stem, fruit, habitat, or other (which is kinda a mix of this or roots or whatever doesn’t fit in the other categories). Well worth your time! I probably wouldn’t recommend any other plant ID app this one really takes the cake. I have already recommended this app to a ton of other people, and they like it, too. If you’re looking for a plant ID app, and you’re not sure or feeling hopeless with the search, give this one a try it just might surprise you.

Either accurate or helps narrow things down. This is the best app for plant ID I’ve used so far. It’s impossible to be 100% accurate from just a picture, given how many little subspecies there are for any given plant, but in the context that while this is not a replacement for scientifically keying something out, this does a fantastic job of giving you a reasonable range of options, usually getting pretty close the first time.

It’s a good mix of machine ID, and supplementary crowd sourced info.
